The parent sequence is incorporated as an initial condition, and we enforce the constraints that the sequence elements are within [0, 1000]. We use the discrete Fourier transform (FFT) to compute the full convolution efficiently. 2. Mathematical specification
The objective is to minimize $\frac{2n \cdot \max(\text{convolve}(a, a)_\text{full})}{\sum(a)^2}$, where $a$ is a sequence of length $n$. We work with sequences normalized such that $\sum(a) = \sqrt{2n}$. The subgradient is computed by identifying active convolution indices at the maximum value and summing the corresponding right endpoint factors. The optimization uses the full linear convolution defined by $\text{convolve}(a, a)_\text{full}[k] = \sum_{m=0}^{n-1} a_m \cdot a_{k-m} \cdot [0 \leq k-m \leq n-1]$. Constraints are enforced by clipping and projecting to the simplex.
